question: An internal communications lead asks Claude to adapt a global announcement for staff at a site that is closing. The draft keeps the upbeat, celebratory framing of the original. What is the most appropriate refinement?
options: A) Rewrite it in a register that fits what this audience is being told, keeping the facts intact.
B) Add a paragraph acknowledging the closure at the end of the otherwise unchanged announcement text.
C) Shorten the announcement so that the celebratory passages take up less space in the message.
D) Keep the celebratory framing, since consistency with the global message matters most here.
correct_answers: A) Rewrite it in a register that fits what this audience is being told, keeping the facts intact.
explanations: Correct. Adapting for an audience means matching the register to their situation, not just their reading level, while every factual statement stays the same.
Incorrect. Appending an acknowledgement after celebratory content reads as an afterthought and does not fix the framing of the piece.
Incorrect. Trimming the upbeat passages leaves the same mismatch in a smaller form and still ignores what the audience is receiving.
Incorrect. Consistency applies to the facts of the announcement, not to a tone that misreads what this audience is being told.
